The $50B rural fund is a temporary band-aid slapped on a self-inflicted wound. The reconciliation bill slashes $911B from Medicaid—hospitals rely on that funding. Now they’re scrambling to offset cuts with a fraction of the lost revenue.

Worse, half the fund gets split equally between states, meaning Connecticut’s 3 rural hospitals could get the same as Kansas’ 90. That’s not efficiency—it’s political theater.

Instead of robbing Peter to pay Paul, fix the root problem: bloated bureaucracy and misplaced priorities. Permanent cuts require permanent solutions, not five-year slush funds.
